decisionBox.changed: The overnight resolved midnight's open question and it resolved AGAINST midnight's stance, but not badly enough to change the structure. Midnight held ADD with a reduce trigger at 79,395.0 and an invalidation at 79,199.0. Both were hit. Price broke to 79,000.0 inside the 07:00 UTC hour - 199 points through the invalidation - and the reduce level fired on the settled 09:00 UTC close of 79,309.9 and again on the 10:00 UTC close of 79,366.3. The flush was violent and one-sided: 1,220,668 USD of liquidations in a single 79,000 bucket across 90 fills, 100 percent long-side, which is the largest one-bucket long flush this series has recorded. Then it held. Price reclaimed 473.9 points off that low and has spent nine hours building a shelf between 79,280 and 79,630, back above the 1H EMA200 at 79,324.50. So the bear case got its move and could not extend it. What has NOT changed - and this is why the tilt stays bearish rather than flipping - is the positioning. Open interest is UP another 0.78 percent since the midnight snapshot, from 2,115,031,593 to 2,131,493,483 USD, while price fell 144 points. That is the third consecutive session of longs adding into weakness, and this time they did it straight through a 1.2m USD liquidation event: the crowd was flushed AND replaced inside the same six hours. The account ratio is unmoved at 1.11 and funding is still fractionally positive. Set against that, the daily chart is untouched - price is 2,693.6 points above the daily EMA20 with all four daily averages stacked bullish and daily RSI at 64.17 - and the dollar is helping for once, with DXY down 0.21 percent to 98.9677. Net: the same range, one liquidation cheaper, with the crowd still leaning the wrong way.

liquidation.note: 1,220,668 USD across 90 filled OKX BTC-USDT-SWAP liquidations, 100 percent LONG-side, all inside the 07:00 UTC hour. This is measured realized-liquidation data, not an estimate, and it is the largest single-bucket flush in this series to date. The pocket has now been struck and price rejected 473.9 points off it, so it is spent leverage rather than resting fuel - but open interest rebuilt straight through it, which means a fresh cohort is sitting above the same level.
15,131 USD across 9 filled liquidations, all LONG-side. A thin shelf on the approach to the 79,000 pocket; it will not stop a move on its own.

549 USD on a single SHORT-side fill. Essentially nothing - there is no short leverage of consequence anywhere above spot in this window, which is exactly what a 1.11 account ratio and positive funding describe.

liquidityMagnet.note: The imbalance is extreme and it points down. Of the 1,236,348 USD of liquidations captured in this window, 1,235,799 USD - 99.96 percent - were LONG-side, against 549 USD short. There is effectively no short leverage above spot to squeeze, while the long side has a proven, freshly-rebuilt pocket at 79,000. Pull is down, but with an important caveat: that pocket has already fired once today, so the fuel below is newly-laid rather than accumulated, and the 79,000 print itself is now a defended level rather than an untested one.

calibration.rollingRecord: Midnight held ADD with reduceIf 79,395.0 and invalidatesAt 79,199.0. Both triggered. The reduce fired on the settled 09:00 UTC close of 79,309.9 and confirmed on the 10:00 UTC close of 79,366.3; the invalidation was breached inside the 07:00 UTC hour on the 79,000.0 low, 199 points through. Acting on the reduce trigger helped in the narrow sense that it flagged the break before the low, though the subsequent 473.9-point reclaim means a trader who reduced and did not re-enter is now behind spot. Midnight's addIf at 80,075.0 did not fire - the session high was 79,627.5, some 447.5 points short.
calibration.note: Two sessions running, the levels have been mechanically correct and the directional stance has been early. Midnight's own bias review said the same thing about endday. The pattern worth naming: this range keeps paying the level-reader and punishing the position-taker, which argues for smaller tranches and more patience rather than sharper levels.
